target_customer: Brazilian companies (new-economy startups and enterprises) needing bank accounts, payments and corporate cards via API
problem: Brazilian banks offered no banking API; companies had to run payables and receivables through slow web banking or manual files.
business_model: Fees per payment method on cash management plus take rate on corporate-card transactions; banking-as-a-service planned

founders.name: Rafael Stark
education: Engineering graduate (ITA); studied in the US
previous_startups: Hummingbird (software house building digital products for Nextel and Banco Paulista)
founders.background_notes: Returned to Brazil in 2014 per Bloomberg Linea; YC lists him as sole founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: A bank API on top of Brazilian payment rails plus central-bank authorization (SCD licence granted Oct 2020) is standard engineering with a heavy regulatory component.

defensibility.rationale: The SCD licence (Forbes Brasil, Oct 2020) and integration into customer ERPs raise copying costs, but licences were obtainable by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying the API wedge by 2022; Bloomberg Linea in 2022 lists Cora and Loft among Stark clients.

market_need_then: Founder said he built the API because a client needed bank-transfer automation no bank offered (Forbes Brasil, Oct 2020); clients included Loft, Rappi, Buser, Kovi and Colgate by Oct 2020.

identity.logo: STARK BANK wordmark in YC listing (not described in sources)

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the brand itself; the name coincides with the founder's surname but no source states that was the reason.

outcome_analysis: Stark Bank began as a bank API for companies in 2018, earned a central-bank SCD licence in October 2020 and signed marquee fintech clients such as Loft and Cora. It raised a roughly 13M USD Series A in December 2021 and a 45M Series B led by Ribbit and Bezos Expeditions in April 2022, which signals strong traction in a market lacking developer-friendly banking. It remains active with about 70 staff; later rounds, if any, were not found.
notes: Series A amount: headline US$13M, body R$74M (about US$13.1M per a second outlet). Dealroom/PitchBook claim 58-59M total over four rounds, so an earlier round (a Contxto headline mentions a raise over US$1M) is likely missing: coverage partial. No competitor source dated near W20 was found (later articles name Brex, Ramp, Marqeta as benchmarks, not 2020 competitors). Name origin searched, nothing found. Founder background beyond Rafael Stark not found; YC page lists one founder.
